blocks.explanation: The volume's argument in one sheet: that intent is invariant, substrate-independent, and capable of persisting across absolute loss of context, deep time, and duality itself. The Invariance Theorem asks, given disjoint realization manifolds and their realization operators, whether an equivalence class of realizations exists for which the semantic deviation vanishes — meaning semantic identity is fully decoupled from material location or composition. The central phenomenon is context collapse: observations vanish, environmental constraints collapse, the physical substrate decays and kinetic energy goes to zero, yet because intent is an independent primitive on the semantic manifold, the collapse of local physical Lagrangians does not erase it — the system transitions from active living to pure persisting. Three parts follow: mathematics (decoupling distance metrics, substrate migration via TransEg, topological invariants of memory), thermodynamics (zero-point thermodynamics, alien semantics with zero shared context, deep-time entropy pumping), and transcendence (voluntary context loss as samadhi or fana, and the Nasadiya threshold). The trilogy summary table sets the existence, stability and invariance problems side by side.
blocks.tts: Volume Three, the invariance problem. When observation, environment, substrate and energy all go to zero, the semantic object survives the collapse. Persistence is not the survival of matter — it is the invariance of meaning.
